items.title: Lowering the level of a degree p extension of discretely valued fields by a totally ramified separable base change
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter more-algebra.tex (More on Algebra)
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file more-algebra.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma is the level-lowering step of the elimination-of-ramification argument: for discrete valuation rings A contained in B contained in C with fraction fields K contained in L contained in M, with A of mixed characteristic (0, p), A in B weakly unramified, B containing a primitive p-th root of 1 and the residue field of A equal to the intersection of the p-power residue fields of B, a degree p extension M/L of positive finite level l can be brought to level at most max(0, l - 1, 2l - p) after a finite separable base change of K that is totally ramified with respect to A, unless that base change is already a weak solution (statement lines 35166-35179). The argument is not a citation: it first converts the polynomial presenting M/L into the polynomial z^p - z modulo two explicitly computed error terms, one for the value and one for the multiplicative correction law, and chooses the exponent m so that those errors land exactly on the target level (proof lines 35190-35209). The core is an induction on the number of coefficients of xi that lie outside the residue field of A: pairs of indices related by a power of p are removed by an explicit correction of the generating element, and in the remaining case a base change of degree p^r obtained by extracting a p^r-th root of a uniformizer is performed and the computation is redone in the integral closure, so that the new level is read off from an expansion rather than from a general principle (proof lines 35282-35366). The degenerate case in which all coefficients lie in the residue field of A is closed by a contradiction with the minimality of n, using that the residue field of A is perfect, and then by an explicit degree p extension of K (proof lines 35234-35280); the level invariant, the p-power-orbit reduction and the p^r base change together are what put this beyond routine technique.
